page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7se.6xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 12 physical Intel Xeon 8369B cores operating at a clock speed of 2.9 GHz. The system architecture is x86_64, supported by 96.0 GB of system memory, which translates to a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage options.

Performance benchmarks place the ecs.g7se.6xlarge in the average tier across most standardized tests. The instance achieved a single-core stress-ng CPU score of 1859.78 and a multi-core score of 23314.73. Its memory subsystem demonstrates a read-only bandwidth of 1273.15 GB/sec for cached small blocks, dropping to 133.42 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, alongside a write bandwidth of 65.35 GB/sec. In application-specific workloads, it processes 23.6 million Redis SET operations per second and delivers a static web serving throughput of 25.78 GB/sec. Notably, its text generation speed for a small 135M parameter LLM model is strong at 286.19 tokens/second, though prompt processing for the same model sits at an average of 1840.19 tokens/second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.g7se.6xlarge offers a balanced resource density for enterprise workloads that require dedicated CPU execution without the premium of specialized memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware. The lack of bundled local storage means storage costs are externalized to network volumes, which is a key architectural tradeoff. This instance is well-suited for general-purpose enterprise applications, software compilation, database operations, and moderate web serving.
